ns2:section.sectionText: The subject of music and politics is a far-ranging topic. To what extent can musical works be regarded as distanced from the cultural context and political environment of their genesis? How can we best evaluate the political implications of works stemming from earlier periods? How do we access the relation of musical and dramatic works to cultural critique and revolutionary currents? The present course focuses not on the political or ceremonial use of music in general, but rather on the relationship of major musical artworks to changing political currents. The emphasis in this seminar falls on the periods from the outbreak of the French Revolution in 1789 to the present day.
